Not physical vibration: static and dynamic force balance residuals are equal (max per brick, mN: column 10.974 static / 10.9739 dyn on brick2; cantilever 22.3988 / 22.3972 on brick2; bridge 24.6456 / 24.6493 on brick2), m*a_com is at most 0.0106 mN; brick motion is at float32 resolution (peak-to-peak displacement up to 0.0112 um column, 0.0149 um cantilever, 0.0086 um bridge; velocity max 0.0062, 0.0047, 0.0029 mm/s); the dominant FFT peaks of displacement/velocity sit at 1.0-46.0 Hz (variance share 0.015-0.291), none near the weld reference 1/(2 pi tc) = 76.4 Hz (tc = max(0.002, 2 dt) = 0.002083 s, dt 0.001042 s). Not a pose-pairing bug: solve-time d.xpos/xmat/xipos ('matched') vs Newton body_q ('unmatched') changes the patch moment by at most 1.5071e-06 (column), 3.7182e-06 (cantilever), 1.7381e-06 (bridge) mN.m and u by at most 1.0420e-09, 1.0203e-08, 4.8067e-09, against moment residuals of 0.0496, 0.3588, 0.1450 mN.m: 4.5, 5.0, 4.9 orders smaller; the Jacobian-transpose force residual is at most 2.7e-17, 6.8e-07, 6.0e-05 mN against force residuals of 10.97, 22.40, 24.65 mN. Cause: the MuJoCo-Warp float32 GPU solve returns weld forces that disagree with CPU double MuJoCo from the same 60 states (CPU tolerance 1e-06, 15 iterations, contacts off): max force-balance residual CPU 7.15e-07 mN vs GPU 3.674 (column), 18.008 (cantilever), 24.460 (bridge) mN; efc force CPU-GPU max 0.003656, 0.010977, 0.015118 and qacc CPU-GPU max 0.058664, 0.105527, 0.450113 (column, cantilever, bridge; qacc CPU max 0.138381, 0.105527, 0.682099).
